headings.title: Introduction and Scope of Skilled Care
headings.content: Skilled care refers to medical services provided by trained healthcare professionals, such as registered nurses and physical therapists, that require specialized clinical knowledge and judgment. Unlike custodial care, which focuses on assistance with activities of daily living like bathing and dressing, skilled care addresses complex medical conditions needing continuous monitoring and technical execution. In the Nigerian healthcare landscape, this level of care is increasingly vital within specialized geriatric centers, post-surgical step-down units, and long-term care facilities where patients transition from acute hospital admissions. Recognizing the distinct boundaries between basic support and professional clinical intervention ensures proper resource allocation and prevents adverse patient outcomes.

headings.title: Core Principles and Objectives
headings.content: The delivery of skilled care rests on maintaining patient safety, promoting optimal recovery, preventing secondary complications, and preserving individual dignity. Every clinical action is guided by evidence-based protocols aimed at restoring pre-morbid health status or stabilizing chronic degenerative illnesses. Objectives must be measurable and tailored to the individual rather than generalized facility routines.

headings.title: Spectrum of Skilled Nursing Interventions
headings.content:
- **Wound Management**: Assessment and treatment of complex surgical incisions, pressure ulcers, and chronic venous leg ulcers using sterile technique and specialized dressings.
- **Tube Feedings**: Administration of enteral nutrition and hydration via nasogastric or gastrostomy tubes, accompanied by residual volume checks and site care.
- **Tracheostomy Care**: Suctioning, inner cannula cleaning, and stoma site maintenance to ensure a patent airway and prevent infection.
- **Catheter Maintenance**: Insertion, monitoring, and periodic changing of indwelling urinary catheters alongside strict output measurement.

headings.title: The Interdisciplinary Care Team
headings.content:
Providing holistic skilled care requires seamless collaboration among diverse health professionals. The registered nurse often serves as the central coordinator, synthesizing inputs from physicians, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, and social workers.

| Team Member | Primary Clinical Focus |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Physician / Medical Officer** | Diagnosis, medical treatment plans, and overall prognosis |
| **Registered Nurse** | Direct clinical care, symptom monitoring, and care coordination |
| **Physiotherapist** | Mobility restoration, muscle strengthening, and gait training |
| **Dietitian** | Nutritional assessment, caloric calculations, and therapeutic diets |

headings.title: Comprehensive Patient Assessment and Care Planning
headings.content: A structured admission assessment forms the bedrock of skilled care. Nurses evaluate physiological systems alongside cognitive status, nutritional reserves, and environmental safety risks. Findings feed directly into the nursing care plan, a dynamic document that outlines prioritized diagnoses, targeted interventions, and evaluation timelines. In busy Nigerian clinical settings, maintaining an updated care plan prevents critical omissions during shift handovers.

headings.title: Medication Administration and Clinical Safety
headings.content: Administering medications in skilled care environments demands rigorous adherence to safety protocols due to the multi-drug regimens common among elderly or chronically ill residents. Nurses must verify the five rights, assess renal and hepatic clearance indicators, and monitor for adverse drug interactions. Advanced clinical procedures, such as intravenous therapy administration and blood glucose monitoring, require meticulous technique to avoid complications like extravasation or infection.

headings.title: Rehabilitation, Restorative Care, and Functional Maintenance
headings.content: Restorative nursing bridges the gap between formal physical therapy and daily living. Nurses incorporate rehabilitation principles into routine activities, encouraging residents to feed themselves, participate in transfers, and maintain joint mobility. Preventing contractures, skin breakdown, and muscle atrophy relies heavily on consistent repositioning schedules and early mobilization protocols.

headings.title: Documentation, Legal Standards, and Quality Assurance
headings.content: Accurate, contemporaneous documentation protects both the patient and the healthcare provider. In skilled care, records must reflect clinical reasoning, patient responses, and communication with the medical team. Adherence to professional codes of conduct and legal standards ensures accountability. Quality assurance programs utilize these records to audit care delivery, identify systemic gaps, and drive continuous clinical improvement.
